subject: physics

source.track: IGCSE · ages 14–16 · all candidates study Core; Extended candidates also study the Supplement

note: Units follow the syllabus's six numbered subject-content sections (1–6), taught in order. Core material anchors the foundational and intermediate lessons; Supplement (Extended-only) material feeds the advanced and expert lessons.

program.title: Motion, forces and energy
topics: 1.1 Physical quantities and measurement techniques
1.2 Motion
1.3 Mass and weight
1.4 Density
1.5 Forces (1.5.1 Effects of forces, 1.5.2 Turning effect of forces, 1.5.3 Centre of gravity)
1.6 Momentum
1.7 Energy, work and power (1.7.1 Energy, 1.7.2 Work, 1.7.3 Energy resources, 1.7.4 Power)
1.8 Pressure

program.title: Thermal physics
topics: 2.1 Kinetic particle model of matter (2.1.1 States of matter, 2.1.2 Particle model, 2.1.3 Gases and the absolute scale of temperature)
2.2 Thermal properties and temperature (2.2.1 Thermal expansion, 2.2.2 Specific heat capacity, 2.2.3 Melting, boiling and evaporation)
2.3 Transfer of thermal energy (2.3.1 Conduction, 2.3.2 Convection, 2.3.3 Radiation, 2.3.4 Consequences of thermal energy transfer)

program.title: Waves
topics: 3.1 General properties of waves
3.2 Light (3.2.1 Reflection, 3.2.2 Refraction, 3.2.3 Thin lenses, 3.2.4 Dispersion)
3.3 Electromagnetic spectrum
3.4 Sound

program.title: Electricity and magnetism
topics: 4.1 Simple phenomena of magnetism
4.2 Electrical quantities (4.2.1 Electric charge, 4.2.2 Electric current, 4.2.3 Electromotive force and potential difference, 4.2.4 Resistance, 4.2.5 Electrical energy and electrical power)
4.3 Electric circuits (4.3.1 Circuit diagrams and circuit components, 4.3.2 Series and parallel circuits, 4.3.3 Action and use of circuit components)
4.4 Electrical safety

4.5 Electromagnetic effects (4.5.1 Electromagnetic induction, 4.5.2 The a.c. generator, 4.5.3 Magnetic effect of a current, 4.5.4 Force on a current-carrying conductor, 4.5.5 The d.c. motor, 4.5.6 The transformer)

program.title: Nuclear physics
topics: 5.1 The nuclear model of the atom (5.1.1 The atom, 5.1.2 The nucleus)
5.2 Radioactivity (5.2.1 Detection of radioactivity, 5.2.2 The three types of nuclear emission, 5.2.3 Radioactive decay, 5.2.4 Half-life, 5.2.5 Safety precautions)

program.title: Space physics
topics: 6.1 The Earth and the Solar System (6.1.1 The Earth, 6.1.2 The Solar System)
6.2 Stars and the Universe (6.2.1 The Sun as a star, 6.2.2 Stars, 6.2.3 The Universe)
